sentences.text: Kaiwhekea is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous of what is now New Zealand.
This animal was approximately 6.5 to 7 meters long.
The holotype specimen was found inside a concretion weighing an estimated 10 tons.
The skeleton is preserved mostly as negative moulds because the original mineralized bone was too fragile to survive.
The holotype of Kaiwhekea was discovered in 1983 by amateur fossil collector Gary Raper at Shag Point, Otago.
The genus name Kaiwhekea translates to 'squid-eater' from Māori words meaning 'food' and 'squid'.
Kaiwhekea has been classified as an aristonectine plesiosaur closely related to Aristonectes.
Kaiwhekea belongs to the parent group Weddellonectia.
Kaiwhekea is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
In 2010, Kaiwhekea was transferred to the family Leptocleididae, but recent analyses do not support this placement.
Kaiwhekea lived around 70 to 69 million years ago.
The time range for Kaiwhekea spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
